votes.reasoning: The dedupe filter in addGuests.handler.ts uses strict equality: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` while the blacklist comparison lowercases (`email.toLowerCase()`, `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). Neither lowercases the guest input, so 'User@Example.com' vs 'user@example.com' would bypass both dedupe and blacklisting, creating a duplicate BookingAttendee row and sending duplicate emails. Whether the DB consistently stores lowercase emails cannot be verified from the diff, so confidence is low, but the mechanism is clearly present in the added code.

judged_text: Case-insensitivity miss in attendee dedupe check allows duplicate attendee rows via case variants

record.issue_text: Case-insensitivity miss in attendee dedupe check allows duplicate attendee rows via case variants

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the dedupe/blacklist logic compares emails case-sensitively: `guest === attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without normalizing `guest`/`attendee.email` (while the blacklist is lowercased). This allows adding duplicates via case variants (e.g., `Test@x.com` vs `test@x.com`) and can create duplicate attendee rows via `attendees.createMany`.
